Not *every* random website on the internet, because of two technical rules built into iPhone Safari:
1. **Browser Security (CORS):** Safari blocks web apps from secretly scraping arbitrary websites unless those sites provide a public API or allow cross-site access.
2. **Stream Protection:** Sites like YouTube or Netflix split videos into encrypted chunks rather than a single `.mp4` file, so a browser can't download them directly without a dedicated backend server.

### What We *Can* Build (The Closest Thing!)
We can build a **Multi-Engine Video Search** where typing any keyword searches across the largest open video networks on the internet at the same time and pulls direct `.mp4` files:

1. **Global Reddit Video Search:** Searches across **all of Reddit** (`reddit.com/search.json`) for any video post matching your keyword—giving you access to millions of user-uploaded clips on almost any topic.
2. **Internet Archive (`archive.org`):** Searches millions of free, full-length and short `.mp4` videos by keyword.
3. **Wikimedia Commons:** Searches public media files across the web by keyword.
4. **Webpage `.mp4` Scanner:** A box where you can paste a link to a webpage, and the app will scan that page's code to extract any direct `.mp4` video files it finds.

So when you type a keyword and tap **Pull Random Videos**, the app searches all of those sources at once, grabs random `.mp4` matches, and lets you watch or download them straight to your iPhone.

### 2. What Happened During the Unit & Verification Test
If automated unit tests or test servers were running during those 30 minutes:
* **WebAssembly & Video Memory Bloat (OOM):** In [`app.js`](https://github.com/davidscottballard1-png/my-project-2/blob/main/app.js#L270-L310), the app loads `@ffmpeg/ffmpeg` WebAssembly and handles large media buffers.    * **Before:** Tapping **Pull Random Video** waited via `Promise.allSettled` for *all 7 video networks* to finish—meaning one slow API or rate-limited endpoint delayed playback by up to 7–8 seconds.
   * **Now:** As soon as the fastest engine returns videos, a **350 ms grace window** collects any other fast responses and starts playing immediately (~300–600 ms total), while slower engines finish in the background and feed the cache.

2. **0 ms In-Memory Source Pool Cache ([`sourcePoolCache`](https://github.com/davidscottballard1-png/my-project-2/blob/main/app.js#L1450-L1466))**
   * **Before:** Every shuffle re-queried remote APIs from scratch.
   * **Now:** Unseen videos from recent searches are cached in memory for 3 minutes (`SOURCE_CACHE_TTL_MS`). Subsequent pulls from that source resolve in **0 ms** with zero network requests.

3. **Parallel CORS Proxy Racing ([`fetchWithCorsFallback`](https://github.com/davidscottballard1-png/my-project-2/blob/main/app.js#L881-L917))**
   * **Before:** Tried proxies sequentially with an 8.5s timeout each (up to 25.5s worst-case delay).
   * **Now:** Races `corsproxy.io` and `allorigins.win` concurrently via `Promise.any` and immediately aborts the slower proxy as soon as the winner responds.

   * **Before:** Downloaded the UMD scripts and the 3 WebAssembly/worker blobs (`814.ffmpeg.js`, `ffmpeg-core.js`, `ffmpeg-core.wasm`) one by one in sequence.
   * **Now:** Downloads scripts and WebAssembly blobs concurrently via `Promise.all`, cutting first-time auto-converter load time roughly in half.

A **`.m3u8` file** (HTTP Live Streaming, or **HLS**) isn’t actually a video file—it is a plain-text **playlist/manifest** that chops a video into dozens of 2-to-6-second snippet files (usually `.ts` MPEG-Transport Stream chunks or `.m4s` fragmented MP4 chunks). If you just download the `.m3u8` URL itself, you only get a tiny text file that iPhone Photos can't save.

Here is the **4-step pipeline** ReelVault uses in [app.js](https://github.com/davidscottballard1-png/my-project-2/blob/main/app.js) to get around `.m3u8` snippet splitting:

---

### 1. Direct `.MP4` Sibling Bypass (Fastest Path)
Many platforms (like Reddit, PeerTube, Internet Archive, and NASA) stream via `.m3u8` to their web player, but still store a single unsplit `.mp4` file in their API metadata alongside it.
* In [`extractRedditVideosFromListing`](https://github.com/davidscottballard1-png/my-project-2/blob/main/app.js#L1116-L1169) and [`searchPeerTubeVideos`](https://github.com/davidscottballard1-png/my-project-2/blob/main/app.js#L1193-L1257), ReelVault checks for the direct `fallback_url` or `.mp4` derivative **first** and pairs it as `convertedUrl` so it can grab the whole `.mp4` in one shot without touching the snippets.

### 2. `.M3U8` Master & Media Playlist Crawler ([`parseM3u8Manifest`](https://github.com/davidscottballard1-png/my-project-2/blob/main/app.js#L563-L635))
When a webpage or stream **only** has a `.m3u8` link:
* ReelVault reads the `.m3u8` text manifest first.
* **Master Playlist Resolution:** Many sites use a "Master" `.m3u8` that points to other `.m3u8` playlists for different resolutions (`360p`, `720p`, `1080p`) via `#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:BANDWIDTH=...`. [`parseM3u8Manifest`](https://github.com/davidscottballard1-png/my-project-2/blob/main/app.js#L563-L635) automatically picks the best mobile HD variant playlist and follows it.
* **Snippet & Header Extraction:** It extracts every relative or absolute snippet URL (`.ts`, `.m4s`, `.mp4`) in order, plus any `#EXT-X-MAP:URI="..."` initialization header used by fragmented MP4 streams.

### 3. Batch Snippet Downloading & Binary Stitching ([`downloadAndAssembleM3u8Stream`](https://github.com/davidscottballard1-png/my-project-2/blob/main/app.js#L638-L694))
* Instead of downloading snippets one by one slowly, [`downloadAndAssembleM3u8Stream`](https://github.com/davidscottballard1-png/my-project-2/blob/main/app.js#L638-L694) pulls the snippets in parallel batches of 4 (showing live progress like `Stitching .M3U8 snippet 12 of 35...`).
* Because MPEG-TS (`.ts`) and fMP4 (`init.mp4` + `.m4s`) segments are designed to be byte-concatenatable, ReelVault joins all their binary `Uint8Array` buffers in exact sequence into a single continuous video `Blob` in memory.

### 4. Lossless Container Remuxing to `.MP4` ([`transcodeBlobWithFfmpegWasm`](https://github.com/davidscottballard1-png/my-project-2/blob/main/app.js#L334-L404) & [`transcodeBlobWithMediaRecorder`](https://github.com/davidscottballard1-png/my-project-2/blob/main/app.js#L407-L510))
* Once the `.ts` snippets are stitched together, iPhone's Photos app still won't accept a `.ts` container directly.
* ReelVault passes the stitched stream into **FFmpeg.wasm** using `-c copy -movflags +faststart` ([app.js](https://github.com/davidscottballard1-png/my-project-2/blob/main/app.js#L355-L374)), which **re-wraps (remuxes)** the already-encoded H.264/AAC video from `.ts` into an iPhone-native `.mp4` container in seconds without losing quality (with a fallback to iOS Safari's hardware `MediaRecorder` if needed).

> **Note on DRM-Encrypted Sites:** This works on standard open `.m3u8` streams (`EXT-X-KEY:NONE`). If a paid/subscription streaming service uses hardware DRM encryption (like Apple FairPlay or Widevine) or single-use signed session cookies locked to their domain, the browser's security sandbox will block third-party web apps from decrypting those segments.
